result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend matched Plex or Noto families, put the Latin face first in the stack, and cover RTL and per-script sizing. B is better because it gives a complete per-script CSS stack with platform-specific system fallbacks and says plainly that it hasn't verified weights or glyph coverage. It also suggests testing with the web fonts blocked. A is solid, but it drifts into general layout and line-breaking advice, and it is less candid about the gaps between platforms. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A gives a concrete per-script CSS stack with named system fallbacks for Arabic and Japanese. It puts the Latin font first so stop names keep the Latin design, uses size-adjust to match x-heights, and openly says it hasn't verified font weights or glyph coverage, adding a test with web fonts blocked. B covers similar ground and adds useful Arabic and Japanese rules such as no letter-spacing and minimum sizes. However, its stack example has no system fallbacks, it says less about what can't be guaranteed across devices, and it drifts further into general line-breaking and layout advice.
